To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
P. multocdia serotype B isolates from buffalo and cattle were genetically similar with other animal species.

the 16S rDNA sequence analysis of the five isolates of P. multucida serotype B2 from different animal species revealed close relationships among the buffalo and cattle isolates with other uncommon hosts.

the P. multocdia serotype B: 2 strains of cattle, pig, and sheep were found to have 99.9 % homology with the P. multicodia serotype B:1 strain of buffalo, while the P. multoicida serotype B2 strain of goat was found to have 98.8% homologous with the vaccine strain of buffalo.

the phylogenetic analysis of P. multodica serogroup B strains isolated from different animal species.
the phylogenetic analysis of P. multodida isolates from different host sources, and the findings will provide a basis for further studies on the pathogenesis and evolution of P. multodia.
the comparative sequence analysis of the 16S rDNA gene of P. multodica serotype B isolates from buffalo, cattle, sheep, pig and goat.

the isolates under investigation are of P. multocide serotype B: 2 and are closely related to the vaccine strain.
the P. multocidal serogroup B is highly host-specific, and the isolates of buffalo are genetically related to the cattle isolates of the same serotype.

P. multocdia isolates belonging to serogroup B are closely related to each other, regardless of their host of origin.
the isolates from different host animals shared 100% homology with each other and also with the type strain.

, P. multocdia serotype B: 2 is capable of causing disease in a wide range of hosts and the isolates from different hosts may be genetically related.
the P. multocidal serogroup B strains from buffalo and cattle are genetically very close and are not very different from strains isolated from other animals.
